This spec exists to re-run the cas vs cas23 dual-socket comparison from
SUMMARY.md finding 4 against the current tree and the best-known cas build
flags (see cmake_flags). The original directory/ and snoop/ trees were
collected with the old CLI run_join.py, one run per point, and before
Keys beginning with '_' are comments and are ignored by run_join.py.
_cmake_flags: The best-known cas configuration: the 2025_INLINE code path (which hoists
the queue cursors into registers across a batch), bucketized 8-slot
cachelines, the AVX-512 simd find, DOUBLE prefetch on the find path
(prefetcht1 at enqueue + prefetcht0 at dequeue) and DOUBLE on the insert
path (CAS_PREFETCH_INSERTION, new in f65f6ac: prefetcht1 at enqueue +
prefetchw at dequeue, so the line arrives exclusive and the CAS pays no
S->E upgrade). UNIFORM_PROBING/GROWT are carried over from amd-9354p.json
so the two machines' trees stay comparable; neither touches cas's or
cas23's inner loop. cas23 (ht-type 8) is unaffected by
CAS_PREFETCH_INSERTION -- it always prefetches for write.
_params: Same x-axes as the original intel dual sets in directory/, so the new
numbers drop straight on top of the old figures.

_reps: SUMMARY.md measures dual-socket run-to-run spread at 2.4% (snoop) to 8%
(directory) on a single point, and cas_vs_cas23_skew_crossover.md section
13c argues 10 reps are the minimum to resolve a 10% effect, which is the

per-point median and throughput_samples every raw run, so the spread is auditable.
